parsed.rationale: Three distinct types — `HSBColor` (package `ColorPalette`, `Shared/ColorPalette/Sources/ColorPalette/HSBColor.swift:31`), `AccentColor` (package `Wallpaper`, `Shared/Wallpaper/Sources/Wallpaper/Core/ThemeColors.swift:62`), and `HSBOffset` (package `Wallpaper`, `Shared/Wallpaper/Sources/Wallpaper/Core/ThemeColors.swift:198`) — all expose an exactly-duplicated initializer `init(hue:saturation:brightness:)`. Introducing a protocol `HSBInitializable` with that initializer requirement in the `ColorPalette` package (which `Wallpaper` already depends on, given it uses HSB concepts) would unify the contract, allow generic code to construct any conforming type, and make the shared semantic intent explicit. The `Wallpaper` package's `AccentColor` and `HSBOffset` would then declare conformance, and any shared factory or conversion logic could be written once against the protocol. None of the records carry test, codegen, mock, or sample-app flags, so this is live production code where the duplication is unintentional.
